summary: Unexpected US egress after enabling VPC-residency pinning (DNS + connection reuse interaction)
summary_detail: Customer reports sporadic increases in p95/p99 API latency and traffic observed in US edges after they flipped on VPC-based strict residency pinning for EU workloads. Appears correlated with long-lived HTTP/2 connection reuse by their corporate proxy + DNS prerendering in their environment.
description:
Issue summary:
Mediscope enabled "strict" residency pinning for their private VPC deployment (eu-west) on 2026-03-09 to meet data residency audit. After the change they see ~1-2% of requests routed to US edges, causing p95 spikes and additional egress cost. Customer is concerned this violates residency guarantees.

Impact:
- Intermittent cross-region egress to us-central for eu-west workloads (customer-visible logs and Sentry traces).
- P95 latency increases from ~200ms -> 650-1,200ms for affected requests.
- Regulatory risk for health data.

Environment:
- Private deployment with VPC peering and customer-managed DNS / corporate proxy.
- Region: eu-west (primary).
- Control plane residency mode: strict-pin (TTL 60s).

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Customer issues requests from internal app behind corporate proxy that performs DNS prerender + HTTP/2 connection pooling.
2) Occasionally the proxy reuses an existing connection that was originally established to a different edge (us-central) before the strict-pin was applied.
3) The reused connection omits the token-scoped residency header (X-RW-Residency) on the forwarded request due to header filtering on reuse.
4) Control plane treats the request as unpinned and routes to default global edge (us-central) leading to cross-region egress.

Relevant logs / snippets provided by customer:
- client-side trace: 2026-03-11T14:12:02Z request_id=abc123 url=/v1/generate proxy_conn_id=conn-44 reused=true header_count=12
- edge access log (us-central): 2026-03-11T14:12:02Z src=proxy-ip:45112 dst=edge-us-1 rw-token=masked residency=none route=default
- control-plane audit: 2026-03-11T14:12:03Z token=tok-xxxx resolved_residency=eu-west but incoming_metadata.residency_header_missing=true

Customer-provided hypothesis:
They believe their proxy's connection reuse is stripping or not forwarding the residency header on subsequent requests, creating a race against the control-plane pin-refresh window.

Attachments provided:
- tcpdump of proxy behavior (sensitive)
- aggregated access logs showing matching timestamps
- screenshot of console pin status for tenant
investigation_notes:
Investigation so far:
- Reproduced similar behavior in staging by simulating a proxy that reuses connections established before a pin update; when the X-RW-Residency header is absent we observe routing to default global edge.
- Confirmed control plane fallback behavior: if token-scoped residency header is not present, routing uses token metadata + runtime pin; when a request arrives without header during a pin-refresh window, the request may be sent to another region until the pin is re-established on the session.
- Looked at proxy logs: some client-side proxies reuse long-lived HTTP/2 connections even after DNS changes; if header set is applied only on the initial request, subsequent requests may omit optional headers.
- Noted the pin TTL customer uses (60s) is low; combined with connection reuse it increases probability of mismatch.

Hypotheses:
1) Header omission on reused connections is the proximate cause.
2) Short pin TTL + control plane pin refresh race increases odds of seeing unpinned requests.
3) Customer's DNS prerender/cache behavior can cause connections to open to non-local edges before pin flips, creating existing connection pool to wrong edge.
next_steps:
- Ask SRE networking to validate whether control plane can honor token-scoped residency by inspecting token at TLS layer for reused upstream connections (risk/feasibility).
- Recommend customer increase pin TTL temporarily to 3600s while they remediate proxy behavior.
- Provide customer with a recommended proxy configuration snippet to preserve residency headers across reused connections and to disable cross-region prerendering.
- Add instrumentation to console to surface number of requests lacking residency header per token per region for easier debugging.
- If reproducible, propose a control-plane guard to drop requests without residency header for customers with private strict-pin (opt-in) to avoid accidental egress.
customer_communication:
2026-03-10: Maya Chen -> Mediscope (initial ticket) - Asked for logs, sample request IDs, and confirmation of proxy vendor/version.
2026-03-11: Customer uploaded tcpdump and confirmed corporate proxy is 'EdgeProxy v2.4' with HTTP/2 pooling enabled.
2026-03-12: Diego Ramos -> Customer - Shared staging repro steps and suggested increasing pin TTL to 3600s as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-12: Customer applied TTL change and reported 90% reduction in observed US-egress events during monitoring window (24h).
comments: Diego Ramos (2026-03-11): Spun up staging repro simulating header drop. Confirmed identical routing behavior when header missing.

SRE-Team (2026-03-12): Control plane currently trusts residency header when present, but does not enforce drop for missing header during strict-pin in private deployments. Filing INT follow-up to evaluate safety of stricter enforcement.
Maya Chen (2026-03-12): Customer requests timeline for permanent fix; flagged as compliance-impacting so high priority.
Security (2026-03-13): Need to confirm any proposed control-plane enforcement change will not cause request loss for legitimate edge cases. Recommend feature gated opt-in for now.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: advised customer to increase pin TTL to 3600s and deploy proxy config change to preserve X-RW-Residency header across connection reuse. Customer reported significant reduction in cross-region egress within 24h.
Longer-term action items: SRE to evaluate opt-in enforcement of residency-header presence for private strict-pin customers (INT ticket opened). Add console telemetry for missing residency headers per token.
Status: customer mitigation accepted; engineering follow-up in progress.
